h1: Profile machining centres, copy routers and end milling machines for aluminum and PVC windows
intro: Before a window frame is assembled, its profiles are machined for the hardware — lock and handle places, hinge and espagnolette slots, drainage slots — and its mullions are end-milled to fit the frame. NovoTech supplies these machines from Plastmak, built in Bursa, Turkey, from template-guided to fully automatic: copy routers that follow a template (the SÇ 501, 502S and 512 with triple drilling units, the SÇ 521S for drainage slots and the SÇ 542 for aluminum); the SÇ 211 and SÇ 211S end milling machines; the SÇ 5000 and SÇ 5000S 3-axis CNC drilling and milling machines with three spindles; and the SÇ 4550, a 9-axis machining and cutting centre that takes profiles up to 21′ 4″ (6,500 mm) from a magazine and delivers them machined, cut and labelled. Supplied with a CSA-approved panel, installed and supported from Mississauga, ON, Canada.
hero_points: SÇ 4550: 9 axes, 10 spindles, profiles 78-3/4″ – 255-7/8″, cut at 30° – 150°
SÇ 5000 · 5000S: 3-axis CNC, 3 spindles at 18,000 rpm, travel 15-3/8 × 7-7/8 × 7-7/8″
Copy routers SÇ 501 · 502S · 512 · 521S · 542 · end mills SÇ 211 · 211S, cutters to Ø6-5/16″

groups.title: End milling machines
groups.lead: Mullion (transom) ends milled to the contour of the frame profile.

faq.a: A copy router repeats a cut-out from a template: quick to set up, inexpensive, ideal for a few profile systems. A CNC is programmed instead — new hardware or a new profile system is a new program, not a new template — and the SÇ 5000 and 5000S make every cut-out of a profile in one clamping, the SÇ 5000S from DXF drawings. The SÇ 4550 adds a magazine, cutting and labelling for unattended work.

faq.q: What does an end milling machine do?
faq.a: It cuts the end of a mullion (transom) to the shape of the frame profile it meets, so the T-joint closes tight and can be screwed. A stack of cutters matching the profile does it in one pass; the SÇ 211S changes the whole stack with one button when the profile series changes and mills at angles from −45° to +45°.

The SÇ 502S, 512, 542, 5000S, 4550 and 211S work on aluminum as well as PVC, with 18,000 rpm spindles and cooling where aluminum needs it; the SÇ 501, 521S and 5000 are for PVC, and the SÇ 211 mills both.

It takes up to seven profiles from its magazine, measures each, clamps it on a 3-axis holding station, grooves, drills, marks and mills it with ten spindles and cuts it with a servo saw at any angle from 30° to 150° — profiles 78-3/4″ to 255-7/8″ long. Finished parts leave on a conveyor with a printed barcode label, and the offcuts go to a cart.

faq.q: What voltage do these machines run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.
